fact: In the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 American Community Survey, homes built in 2010 or later make up 85.1% of the housing in Timnath, 69.2% in Severance, 55.5% in Berthoud, 50.3% in Wellington, 46.6% in Windsor, 43.6% in Firestone, 42.8% in Frederick and 41.4% in Johnstown.
quote: Table B25034, ACS 2024 5-year (2020-2024): Timnath, CO — "Total:" 3308; "Built 2020 or later" 760; "Built 2010 to 2019" 2056. Severance, CO — "Total:" 3426; "Built 2020 or later" 843; "Built 2010 to 2019" 1528. Berthoud, CO — "Total:" 5158; "Built 2020 or later" 938; "Built 2010 to 2019" 1925. Wellington, CO — "Total:" 4210; "Built 2020 or later" 310; "Built 2010 to 2019" 1806. Windsor, CO — "Total:" 15463; "Built 2020 or later" 1642; "Built 2010 to 2019" 5559. Firestone, CO — "Total:" 6520; "Built 2020 or later" 792; "Built 2010 to 2019" 2053. Frederick, CO — "Total:" 5930; "Built 2020 or later" 590; "Built 2010 to 2019" 1947. Johnstown, CO — "Total:" 7124; "Built 2020 or later" 447; "Built 2010 to 2019" 2504.
source_label: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year estimates, Table B25034 Year Structure Built (via the Census Reporter API)
notes: Queried 2026-09-25 (release acs2024_5yr, years 2020-2024). Shares are our arithmetic: (Built 2020 or later + Built 2010 to 2019) / Total, rounded to one decimal; they match the archive's wf1/towns-larimer.md figures. B25034 counts all housing units, not only detached houses, and ACS estimates carry margins of error (Timnath's total is 3308 +/- 236). Housing-age statistics only; no income or population figures are used.

fact: The Colorado Geological Survey's homeowner guide says the excavation around a new house is usually refilled with loose soil, that this backfill settles over the first few months or years, and that the settling often flattens or reverses the slope next to the foundation so water ponds there.
quote: The excavated area outside the foundation is usually filled with loose soil fill when a house is constructed. This is called the backfill area (Fig. 26). During the first few months or years, this material settles. Often there is enough settlement to reverse or flatten the slope next to the foundation. Reverse or negative drainage will cause ponding of water during precipitation or heavy irrigation.
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey SP-14, Home Landscaping and Maintenance on Swelling Soil (Jochim, 1981; revised fifth printing 1987)
notes: PDF read with curl and pdftotext on 2026-09-25, Maintenance section, p. 22. The sibling record artificial-turf-vs-pavers-concrete.cgs-sp14-backfill-concrete quotes the next paragraph (concrete over uncompacted backfill).

fact: The same guide says a building site should be graded to an engineer's specifications so water drains away from the house, that planted ground should fall at least 5 percent (6 inches in 10 feet) and bare or paved ground at least 1 percent, that 10 percent is the recommended fall within 10 feet of a foundation, and that slopes over 15 percent are not recommended.
quote: When houses are built, the building site should have been graded according to the specifications of a qualified engineer. The main purpose of lot grading is to provide positive drainage away from the house. … Bare or paved areas should maintain a minimum slope of 1 percent (1 to 2 inches of vertical fall for 10 feet of horizontal distance). Since even a small amount of settlement can reverse such a small slope, a much greater slope is desirable. Vegetated areas should maintain a minimum 5 percent slope (6 inches of vertical fall for 10 feet of horizontal distance). … The recommended slope within the first 10 feet of a foundation is 10 percent (12 inches of vertical fall for 10 feet of horizontal distance). Flat slopes limit drainage but steep slopes result in downhill movement and erosion of the soil. For this reason slopes greater than 15 percent are not recommended.
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey SP-14, Home Landscaping and Maintenance on Swelling Soil (Jochim, 1981; revised fifth printing 1987)
notes: Landscaping section, Slope, pp. 10-11. SP-14 names vegetated and bare or paved ground only; it says nothing about artificial turf.

fact: The guide describes swales as shallow depressions that collect rain, snowmelt and excess irrigation water and move it away from the house and off the property, and lists changing a lot's drainage pattern with patios, fences or other obstructions that dam and pond water among the homeowner mistakes behind swelling-soil damage.
quote: Slope drainage can be collected and moved away from the house by ditches and swales. These are simply shallow trenches (ditches) or depressions (swales) which collect and move rainwater, snowmelt, and excess irrigation water away from the house and off the property. … Much of the damage caused by swelling soils is due to lack of timely maintenance by the homeowner. Problems are caused by: … (5) changing the lot drainage pattern by constructing patios, fences or other obstructions that dam and pond water,
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey SP-14, Home Landscaping and Maintenance on Swelling Soil (Jochim, 1981; revised fifth printing 1987)
notes: Surface drainage, p. 14, and Maintenance, p. 22.

fact: Windsor's storm drainage criteria require a subdivision's drainage construction plans to show its channels, ditches and swales, side and rear yard swales included, with their lengths, widths and cross-sections, and a copy of the approved plans goes to the Town for its file.
quote: Where drainage improvements are to be constructed in accordance with the approved Final Drainage Report, the construction plans (on 24" x 36" mylar) shall be submitted for review and approval prior to construction. A reproducible mylar copy of the approved plans will be submitted to the Town for file. The plans and specifications for the drainage improvements will include: … 3. Channels, ditches, and swales (including side/rear yard swales) with lengths, widths, cross-sections, and erosion control (i.e. riprap, concrete, grout) indicated.
source_label: Town of Windsor, Storm Drainage Design Criteria (Community Development Department, Engineering Division, revised July 1, 2020), Sec. 2.3 Construction Drawings
notes: PDF read with curl and pdftotext on 2026-09-25, pp. 2-5 to 2-6. Sec. 2.4 also says the engineer's As-Built drainage plans must be on file before a Certificate of Occupancy is issued. Criteria for subdivision design, not a rule addressed to homeowners.

fact: Johnstown's building department lists residential landscaping, residential fencing and sprinkler systems among work that needs no building permit, keeps a new concrete patio, driveway or walk at least 3 feet from property lines for required drainage, and says side and rear easements are typically at least 5 feet, as shown on the plat or development plans.
quote: Permit Not Required … residential fencing … residential landscaping … sprinkler systems … Pour new concrete patio, driveway, or on-site walk (minimum 3 feet from property lines for required drainage) … Be aware of setbacks and easements (typically 5 feet minimum from side and rear). Reference the land use and development code, plat, or development plans for details.
source_label: Town of Johnstown, Building Permits page (Permit Required and Permit Not Required lists)
notes: Read with curl (browser user agent) on 2026-09-25. The list items are separate lines on the page, joined here with ellipses. A building permit is not the only approval: HOA or metro district review, and Firestone's separate town turf permit, are other rules.

fact: Johnstown's North Ridge design guidelines require a home's landscape plan to be designed by a landscape design professional and the landscaping to go in as soon as weather permits, no later than six months after the first buyer closes.
quote: G. Landscape plans shall be designed by a landscape design professional. See section 3.5.9 for landscape standards. H. Landscaping to be installed as soon as weather permits, but in any event no later than six (6) months after a home is closed by initial buyer.
source_label: North Ridge Design Guidelines, February 23, 2024 (Town of Johnstown PUD design guidelines), Sec. 3.14.1 Single Family Detached Residential Site Design
notes: PDF read with curl and pdftotext on 2026-09-25. Sec. 3.5.9, the large-lot landscape guidelines, separately says lot landscape 'is to be installed within one month of construction completion, weather permitting'; the two lines differ, so an owner should ask the design review committee which date it holds them to.

fact: The same guidelines carry drainage along streets, private drives and swales along property lines, require positive drainage away from foundations, and allow no grading beyond a property's limits unless the adjacent owners agree.
quote: D. Drainage shall be conveyed along dedicated streets, private drives and swales along property lines, or in open space corridors. … 3.1.4 GRADING A. Provide positive drainage away from foundations. B. Site buildings to minimize cut and fill earthwork operations. C. There shall be no grading beyond the limits of each property except as agreed upon by adjacent owners.
source_label: North Ridge Design Guidelines, February 23, 2024, Secs. 3.1.2 Storm Drainage and 3.1.4 Grading

fact: Johnstown posts the PUD and design guidelines for its subdivisions on one page, among them the Thompson Crossing, North Ridge, The Ridge and 2534 design guidelines.
quote: Planned Unit Development (PUD) & Design Guidelines … 2534 Design Guidelines 2 20 19 approved (PDF) STAMPED … North Ridge Design Guidelines 03.24 (PDF) STAMPED … The Ridge Design Guidelines 03.24 (PDF) STAMPED … Thompson Crossing Design Guidelines 0706 (PDF) STAMPED
source_label: Town of Johnstown, Planned Unit Development (PUD) & Design Guidelines page
notes: Read with curl (browser user agent) and WebFetch on 2026-09-25: 27 documents listed, from 2534 to Welty Ridge, plus the Town Design Guidelines and Town Landscape Standards. The page carries no introduction saying which lots each document governs.

fact: Heron Lakes' rules make the builder responsible for building the approved final grade and the site's drainage and for providing a certificate of drainage and topographical accuracy, and make the owner or landscape contractor responsible for keeping that grading intact.
quote: a. The Developer is responsible for the Finished Overlot Grade of the site. The Builder is responsible for constructing the approved final grade, the site’s drainage and providing the certificate of drainage/topographical accuracy. The Owner/landscape contractor is responsible for maintaining the integrity of the grading which may have been adjusted to comply with berming retaining walls drainage, and the landscape requirements of these design standards.
source_label: Berthoud-Heritage Metropolitan District, Heron Lakes Residential Improvement Rules and Regulations (amended June 1, 2026), Sec. 4.6(a), Landscape Grading Requirements
notes: PDF read with curl and pdftotext on 2026-09-25, p. 79. Sec. 4.6(b), that a landscape contractor may not begin without the builder's certificate, is in berthoud-co.heron-berms-drainage.

fact: The Severance Shores metro districts' guidelines allow no interference with or change to the final government-approved drainage and grading plan on any property, and ask that new landscaping keep water flowing away from the foundation and driveways and into the street gutters.
quote: 2.18. Drainage - ARC approval required for any changes affecting drainage. There can be no interference or modification of the final governmental approved drainage and grading plan over any property. When landscaping is installed, it is especially important to ensure that water drains away from the foundation and driveways of the house and that the flow patterns prevent water from flowing under or ponding near or against the house foundation, walkways, sidewalks, and driveways. Water should flow over walkways, sidewalks or driveways, into the street gutters.
source_label: Severance Shores Metropolitan District Nos. 1-4, Residential Improvement Guidelines and Site Restrictions (amended September 5, 2024), Sec. 2.18 Drainage
notes: PDF read with curl and pdftotext on 2026-09-25. The landscape-plan requirement (a drainage and grading plan showing compliance with the municipality-approved plan) is in severance-co.severance-shores-yards.
